---
title: Messaging
icon: Mail
description: Send transactional email, SMS, and push notifications from your project, and fan a single message out to a topic of subscribers.
---

import { ShieldCheck, Server, SquareFunction, Workflow } from 'lucide-react';

Applad's messaging service sends three kinds of message from your project:
**email** (SMTP), **SMS** (Twilio), and **push** notifications (Firebase Cloud
Messaging). You can send a message directly to recipients, or send once to a
**topic** and have every subscriber receive it. Reusable **templates** let you
keep the copy in one place and fill in `{{variables}}` per send.

![The console Messaging tab](/screens/messaging.png)
_Email, SMS and push are sent from the same Messaging service, directly or fanned out to a topic._

Every channel talks to an outside provider, so it only works once that provider
is configured. If you are running Applad yourself, see
[Configuring providers](#configuring-providers) below and the
[self-hosting guide](/self-hosting) for where to set the environment variables.

All routes live under `/v1/messaging` and require [authentication](/build/authentication):
a client session token or a project API key, plus the `x-applad-project` header.
Because sending costs real money and reputation, messaging is usually driven from
your server with an API key rather than from untrusted clients.

<Callout title="Sending is rate limited">
Every `POST` under `/v1/messaging/` is capped at **60 requests per minute per
project**. This is a project-scoped [rate limit](/build/authentication): it is
about what a send costs, not who made it, so an API key and a client session
count against the same bucket. Exceeding it returns `429` with a message about
cost and sender reputation.
</Callout>

## The provider model

Applad does not talk to email/SMS/push networks itself; each channel forwards to
an outside provider you configure. There are two places a provider can be set,
and Applad resolves them in this order:

1. **Per-project providers** (`/v1/messaging/providers`) come first. The **first
   enabled provider of the matching type** for the project wins. This is how one
   project sends through its own account, or uses a provider other than the
   instance default.
2. **Instance-wide environment variables** are the fallback when a project has no
   enabled provider of that type. These are set by whoever runs the server (see
   [Configuring providers](#configuring-providers)).

<Callout type="warn" title="Which sends honour per-project providers">
The per-project resolver is only applied by **recorded messages**
(`/messaging/messages/*`) and **topic sends** (`/messaging/topics/{id}/messages`).
The **direct-send** endpoints (`/messaging/email`, `/messaging/sms`,
`/messaging/push`) and **template sends** (`/messaging/templates/{id}/send`)
always use the instance-wide environment configuration, never a per-project
provider. If you rely on a project's own provider, send through the recorded or
topic routes.
</Callout>

## Send an email

The client SDKs expose `messaging.sendEmail`, which sends immediately and returns
once the provider has accepted (or rejected) the message. Under the hood this is
`POST /v1/messaging/email`, which you can also call directly from your server.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await client.messaging.sendEmail(
  ['alice@example.com'],
  'Welcome to Acme',
  '<h1>Hello</h1><p>Thanks for signing up.</p>',
);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
await client.messaging.sendEmail(
  to: ['alice@example.com'],
  subject: 'Welcome to Acme',
  html: '<h1>Hello</h1><p>Thanks for signing up.</p>',
);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/email \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" \
  -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "to": ["alice@example.com"],
    "subject": "Welcome to Acme",
    "html": "<h1>Hello</h1>"
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

A successful send returns `200` with `{ "status": "sent" }`.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to` | list of strings | yes | One or more recipient addresses. All go in a single message. |
| `subject` | string | yes | Rejected as `to and subject are required` if empty. |
| `html` | string | no | Body, sent with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`. |

This endpoint sends synchronously through the instance-wide SMTP configuration
and only returns once the SMTP server has accepted or rejected the message, so a
provider error surfaces directly as a `500`.

<Callout title="Email needs SMTP configured">
If no email provider is set up, this call fails with `messaging: SMTP not configured`. Configure SMTP as shown in [Configuring providers](#configuring-providers).
</Callout>

## Send an SMS

`POST /v1/messaging/sms` sends a single text message through Twilio.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/sms \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" \
  -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "to": "+15551234567",
    "body": "Your code is 123456"
  }'
```

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to` | string | yes | A single recipient in E.164 form, for example `+15551234567`. |
| `body` | string | yes | The text of the message. |

A successful send returns `200` with `{ "status": "sent" }`. If Twilio is not
configured the call fails with `messaging: Twilio not configured`.

## Send a push notification

`POST /v1/messaging/push` sends a notification to one device token through
Firebase Cloud Messaging.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/push \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" \
  -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "token": "<device-fcm-token>",
    "title": "New message",
    "body": "You have a new message from Alice"
  }'
```

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | string | yes | One FCM device registration token. |
| `title` | string | yes | Notification title. |
| `body` | string | no | Notification body. |

A successful send returns `200` with `{ "status": "sent" }`. If FCM is not
configured the call fails with `messaging: FCM not configured`.

Push uses Firebase Cloud Messaging's legacy HTTP API with the server key. Sending
is to a single device token per call; to reach many devices, subscribe them to a
[topic](#topics-and-subscribers) and send once.

## Recorded messages

The endpoints above send and forget. If you want a stored record of what was
sent (to show a message history, for example), use the `messages` endpoints
instead. They persist the message, send it in the background, and update its
status.

| Channel | Route | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email | `POST /v1/messaging/messages/email` | `to` (list), `subject`, `html`, `draft` |
| SMS | `POST /v1/messaging/messages/sms` | `to`, `body`, `draft` |
| Push | `POST /v1/messaging/messages/push` | `token`, `title`, `body`, `draft` |

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/messages/email \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" \
  -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "to": ["alice@example.com"], "subject": "Receipt", "html": "<p>Thanks</p>" }'
```

This returns `201` with the stored message right away, before delivery finishes:

```json
{
  "id": "6f2a...",
  "projectId": "acme",
  "type": "email",
  "subject": "Receipt",
  "body": "<p>Thanks</p>",
  "recipients": ["alice@example.com"],
  "status": "processing",
  "scheduledAt": null,
  "deliveredAt": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-07-28T10:00:00Z"
}
```

<Callout title="Status is not the send result">
Because delivery happens in the background, a `201` here means the message was
recorded, not that it was delivered. The `status` starts at `processing` and
becomes `sent` or `failed` once the provider responds. Poll the message to see
the outcome. A provider that is not configured leaves the message `failed`, so
this path will not surface a "not configured" error to the caller the way the
direct-send endpoints do.
</Callout>

Pass `"draft": true` to store the message without sending it (its status stays
`draft`).

Every recorded message has these fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Generated message ID. |
| `projectId` | string | Owning project. |
| `type` | string | `email`, `sms`, or `push`. |
| `subject` | string | Email subject, or the push title. Empty for SMS. |
| `body` | string | HTML for email, text for SMS, notification body for push. |
| `recipients` | list of strings | The `to` addresses / number / device token. |
| `status` | string | See the lifecycle below. |
| `scheduledAt` | string or null | RFC 3339 send time. A future value queues the message; see [Scheduled sends](#scheduled-sends). |
| `deliveredAt` | string or null | Set to the send time once `status` becomes `sent`. |
| `createdAt` | string | RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. |

The `status` moves through these states:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `draft` | Stored with `"draft": true`; never sent. |
| `scheduled` | A future `scheduledAt` was given; waiting for the sweep to deliver it. |
| `processing` | Recorded and handed to a background sender. |
| `sent` | The provider accepted it; `deliveredAt` is set. |
| `failed` | The provider rejected it, or no provider was configured. |

Unlike the direct-send endpoints, the recorded routes resolve the project's own
provider first (see [The provider model](#the-provider-model)) and fall back to
the instance configuration. The required body fields still apply per channel:
email requires `subject`, SMS requires `body`, and push requires `title`.

## Scheduled sends

Any recorded send (`/messaging/messages/email`, `/sms`, or `/push`) accepts an
optional `scheduledAt`, an RFC 3339 timestamp:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/messages/email" \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "to": ["user@example.com"],
        "subject": "Your weekly digest",
        "html": "<h1>This week</h1>",
        "scheduledAt": "2026-08-01T09:00:00Z"
      }'
```

The behaviour depends on the value:

- **In the future** — the message is stored with status `scheduled` and is
  **not** sent inline. A sweep on the cron worker runs once a minute, finds
  every message whose `scheduledAt` has passed, and delivers it through the same
  provider resolution as an immediate send. On success the status moves to
  `sent` and `deliveredAt` is stamped; on failure it moves to `failed`.
- **Absent or already in the past** — nothing changes: the message is sent
  immediately in the background, exactly as before.
- **Combined with `"draft": true`** — draft wins. The message is stored `draft`
  and never sent, regardless of `scheduledAt`.

A malformed `scheduledAt` (not RFC 3339) is rejected with `400`.

Because the sweep claims each due message with a status transition
(`scheduled` to `processing`) before delivering, a message is delivered exactly
once even across multiple worker replicas. Timing is minute-granular: a message
is delivered on the first sweep at or after its `scheduledAt`, never before it.
All timestamps are UTC.

Read messages back:

```bash
# List, newest first, with optional ?search= and ?limit=&offset=
curl "https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/messages?limit=25" \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>"

# One message
curl "https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/messages/<msgId>" \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>"

# Delete a message record
curl -X DELETE "https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/messages/<msgId>" \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>"
```

`GET /v1/messaging/messages` returns `{ "messages": [...], "total": <n> }`.

## Topics and subscribers

A **topic** is a named list of recipients. Add subscribers to it, then send once
to reach all of them. Applad picks the channel per subscriber from the shape of
the `target`:

- starts with `+` (for example `+15551234567`): sent as **SMS**
- contains `@` (for example `alice@example.com`): sent as **email**
- anything else: treated as a **push** device token

<Steps>

<Step>
### Create a topic

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/topics \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "product-updates" }'
```
</Step>

<Step>
### Add a subscriber

The `target` is an email, phone number, or device token.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/topics/<topicId>/subscribers \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "target": "alice@example.com" }'
```
</Step>

<Step>
### Send to everyone subscribed

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/topics/<topicId>/messages \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "subject": "This week at Acme", "body": "<p>News</p>" }'
```
</Step>

</Steps>

`GET /v1/messaging/topics` lists topics with their subscribers, and
`GET /v1/messaging/topics/{topicId}` returns one. On a topic send, `body` is
required and `subject` is optional; `subject` is used only for the email
subscribers, while SMS and push subscribers receive `body`. Because a topic
fans out per subscriber, each recipient goes through the project's own provider
for that channel (with the instance-wide fallback), the same resolution as
recorded messages.

The channel is inferred from each subscriber's `target` string, so a topic can
mix all three:

| Target shape | Example | Channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starts with `+` | `+15551234567` | SMS |
| Contains `@` | `alice@example.com` | Email |
| Anything else | `fMEP0...device-token` | Push |

Adding the same `target` twice is a no-op; duplicate subscribers are ignored. If
delivery to one subscriber fails, the send continues to the rest and reports the
first error.

## Templates

Templates hold reusable copy with `{{variable}}` placeholders, so you keep the
wording out of your code. A template has a `type` (`email`, `sms`, or `push`), a
`subject`, and a `body`.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await client.messaging.createTemplate(
  'welcome',
  'email',
  'Welcome, {{name}}',
  '<p>Hi {{name}}, thanks for joining.</p>',
  { variables: ['name'] },
);

await client.messaging.sendTemplate('<templateId>', ['alice@example.com'], {
  name: 'Alice',
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
await client.messaging.createTemplate(
  name: 'welcome',
  type: 'email',
  subject: 'Welcome, {{name}}',
  body: '<p>Hi {{name}}, thanks for joining.</p>',
  variables: ['name'],
);

await client.messaging.sendTemplate(
  templateId: '<templateId>',
  to: ['alice@example.com'],
  variables: {'name': 'Alice'},
);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

On send, every `{{key}}` in the subject and body is replaced with the matching
value from `variables`, and the result goes out on the template's own channel.
For an `sms` or `push` template, each entry in `to` is sent its own message; for
`email`, the whole `to` list goes in one message.

A template has these fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `templateId` | string | no | Supply your own ID, or omit / pass `unique()` to have one generated. |
| `name` | string | yes | Human label; rejected as `name is required` if empty. |
| `type` | string | no | `email`, `sms`, or `push`. Defaults to `email`. |
| `subject` | string | no | Subject line (email) or title (push); supports `{{variables}}`. |
| `body` | string | no | Body; supports `{{variables}}`. |
| `variables` | list of strings | no | Names of the placeholders the template expects. |

The full set of routes is `POST/GET /v1/messaging/templates`,
`GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/messaging/templates/{templateId}`, and
`POST /v1/messaging/templates/{templateId}/send`.

<Callout type="warn" title="Templates use the instance provider">
Template sends always go through the instance-wide provider for the channel, not
a per-project provider. A template is a convenience over the direct-send path, so
if the matching channel is not configured on the instance, the send fails with
the same `not configured` error.
</Callout>

## Configuring providers

Each channel is off until its provider is configured, and returns a clear
`not configured` error otherwise. This matters most when self-hosting, so
nothing sends silently. Set these environment variables on the API and workers
(see the [self-hosting guide](/self-hosting)):

| Channel | Variables | Not-configured error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email (SMTP) | `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT` (default `587`), `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_FROM` (default `noreply@applad.local`) | `messaging: SMTP not configured` |
| SMS (Twilio) | `TWILIO_SID`, `TWILIO_TOKEN`, `TWILIO_FROM` | `messaging: Twilio not configured` |
| Push (FCM) | `FCM_SERVER_KEY` | `messaging: FCM not configured` |

Email needs at least `SMTP_HOST`; SMS needs `TWILIO_SID` and `TWILIO_TOKEN`;
push needs `FCM_SERVER_KEY`.

<Callout type="warn" title="Only SMTP, Twilio and FCM are wired instance-wide">
The instance-wide fallback covers exactly these three providers. The other
providers below (Mailgun, SendGrid, Resend, Vonage, MSG91) are reachable **only**
as [per-project providers](#per-project-providers); there is no environment
variable that turns one of them into the global default.
</Callout>

### Per-project providers

Beyond the instance-wide environment variables, a project can register its own
providers, which take priority over the global config for that project. This lets
one project send through a different account, or use a provider other than the
three instance defaults. Manage them under `/v1/messaging/providers` (`GET`,
`POST`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /{providerId}`). A provider has a `name`, a `type`
(`email`, `sms`, or `push`), a `provider` implementation, and a `config` object.
It is created **enabled**; `PUT` can change `name`, `config`, and `enabled`.

| `type` | `provider` values |
| --- | --- |
| `email` | `smtp`, `mailgun`, `sendgrid`, `resend` |
| `sms` | `twilio`, `vonage`, `msg91` |
| `push` | `fcm` |

The shape of `config` depends on the `provider`:

<Tabs items={['Email', 'SMS', 'Push']}>
<Tab value="Email">

| `provider` | `config` keys |
| --- | --- |
| `smtp` | `host`, `port` (default `587`), `username`, `password`, `from` |
| `mailgun` | `apiKey`, `domain`, `euRegion` (bool), `senderEmail` |
| `sendgrid` | `apiKey`, `senderEmail`, `senderName` |
| `resend` | `apiKey`, `senderEmail`, `senderName` |

</Tab>
<Tab value="SMS">

| `provider` | `config` keys |
| --- | --- |
| `twilio` | `sid`, `token`, `from` |
| `vonage` | `apiKey`, `apiSecret`, `from` |
| `msg91` | `authKey`, `senderId` |

</Tab>
<Tab value="Push">

| `provider` | `config` keys |
| --- | --- |
| `fcm` | `serverKey` |

</Tab>
</Tabs>

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/messaging/providers \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Acme SMTP",
    "type": "email",
    "provider": "smtp",
    "config": { "host": "smtp.example.com", "port": "587",
                "username": "acme", "password": "secret",
                "from": "noreply@acme.com" }
  }'
```

The first **enabled** provider of a given type is used; if a project has none,
messaging falls back to the instance-wide environment configuration above.
Remember that only recorded messages and topic sends consult per-project
providers (see [The provider model](#the-provider-model)).
